narrative: Claude Sonnet 5 driving per-token cost for capable long-horizon agents to roughly a third of flagship sharpens the economic case behind this prediction: cheaper tokens do not remove the need to bound autonomous spend, they raise the volume of loops running, which is the enterprise-token-bill pressure that pushes platforms to expose budgets and caps by default. Today supplies the substrate-cost condition that makes default spend controls more, not less, necessary.
remaining_gap: This is cost context, not a platform shipping the token-budget-and-cap control itself; no agentic coding platform has made caps a default.
